title: Fill Time Exceeded (Steam) (E11)
shortDescription: The Electrolux dryer reports E11 indicating a fault in the steam inlet, which prevents the cycle from completing safely.
fullDescription: Error code E11 on a Electrolux dryer indicates the control board has detected an abnormal condition involving the steam inlet. The board interrupts the running cycle to prevent damage to the appliance, the laundry load, or surrounding wiring. The dryer logs the fault, locks out further operation until power is cycled, and surfaces the E11 banner to alert the user. Although the immediate trigger is the steam inlet, the underlying cause can range from a damaged wiring harness, to an aged sensor returning out-of-spec readings, to a failed relay on the main control board itself. Diagnosis should always begin with the simplest possible cause (loose connectors, lint blockage, recent power events) before escalating to component replacement.

causes.cause: Steam inlet wiring harness loose or chafed
Steam inlet component reached end of service life and is out of spec
Recent power surge or brownout corrupted control board state
Main control board relay or driver circuit has failed

symptoms: Error code E11 flashes on the display
Cycle stops before clothes are dry
Dryer refuses to start a new cycle
Audible beep or chime accompanies the error

fixSteps.title: Power cycle the dryer
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug the dryer from the wall outlet, or switch off the dedicated breaker, for at least five full minutes. This forces the control board to dump any latched fault states. Restore power and start a short timed-dry cycle to confirm whether the E11 error returns.

fixSteps.title: Inspect the steam inlet
fixSteps.instruction: With the dryer unplugged, access the steam inlet per your model's service sheet. Visually inspect for burnt or melted insulation, loose spade connectors, lint build-up, and signs of moisture. Reseat every connector you find and confirm the ground path is intact.

fixSteps.title: Test the steam inlet with a multimeter
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect the steam inlet from the harness and measure resistance or continuity across its terminals. Compare the reading against the value on the model's tech sheet. If the part reads open, shorted, or far outside the documented range, replace it.

fixSteps.title: Replace the steam valve
fixSteps.instruction: Order a model-specific steam valve from an authorized parts supplier. Install the new part using the original mounting hardware, route the harness clear of hot surfaces and moving components, and reassemble the dryer. Run a full timed cycle to confirm the fault clears.

whenToCallPro: If replacing the steam valve does not clear the E11 error, or if you find evidence of burnt traces on the main control board, schedule a certified appliance technician. Internal PCB repair, refrigerant work (heat-pump models), and any 240 V wiring inside the cabinet should not be attempted by a DIYer without the correct training and tooling.

faq.q: Can I keep using the dryer with E11 showing?
faq.a: No - the control board has shut the cycle down for safety. Diagnose and resolve the fault before further use.

faq.q: Will a power cycle permanently clear E11?
faq.a: Only if the trigger was a transient glitch. If the underlying part is failing, the error will return within a few cycles.

faq.q: Is this code covered under warranty?
faq.a: Most major brands cover the main control board for 1 year and sealed-system parts (heat pump) for longer - check your specific warranty card.
